head: b0e778a559fe985426eaea0e5d52f267034e9b36
classification_reasons: The fix touches a security-sensitive gate check (supersedes path validation that gates whether an incident can retire an earlier lesson) — security-relevant validation logic is non-routine even though the diff is small.

The behavior being fixed (index.py never raising on a malformed lesson) was already specified in spec.md but was not actually covered by any pre-existing test before this round — three new crash paths were found by the owner's own fresh-context review, meaning 'code the existing tests already cover' does not hold.

Blast radius is small (3 source files, no schema/contract change, no risk_list item, no guardrail file) but the overall change (0003) has been classified non-routine throughout; a fix round to a gate check inherits that classification.
attempted: Intent: confirmed the three fixes are exactly the three items the owner's review #5452163356 marked 'Fix in this round' (gate.py _supersedes_problem bare-filename validation; index.py never crashing on a bad stale_after/detected.at/non-UTF-8 file; sdlc-maintain.md step 1 also opening '## Unsorted'), and that the six items marked 'can wait for the tag' were correctly left out and recorded under 'Not applied' rather than silently dropped or silently expanded in scope.

Spec and plan: verified the fix brings the implementation into line with behavior spec.md already required ('never raises', 'a supersedes target ... fails') rather than introducing new design, so no spec.md/plan.md update was needed and none was made; confirmed plan.md's file list already named every file this round touches (checks.py, index.py, sdlc-maintain.md, the three test files) — no scope creep into an unplanned file.

Proof: read the final `_supersedes_problem` body line by line against the three new tests (outside-lessons/ traversal via `../secret.txt`, an absolute path that legitimately names a retired lesson inside lessons/, and self-reference) and confirmed each test's input would have passed the old code (Path.joinpath silently discards the lessons_dir prefix for an absolute `supersedes`, and a bare `..`-prefixed value's `.name` differs from itself only after the fix) and is correctly rejected by the new `Path(value).name != value or not _SUPERSEDES_NAME_RE.match(value) or value == lesson_name` guard; read `_read_text` (now catching `UnicodeDecodeError` alongside `OSError`), `_bad_field_shapes` (int `stale_after`, month-13 `detected.at`) and the hardened `_month_label`/`_date_only` against the four new `tests/test_lessons.py` cases and confirmed each reproduces a path that raised before the fix and is now routed to `## Unsorted` with a note; read the `sdlc-maintain.md` step-1 diff adding '## Unsorted' to the opened set and the matching instruction-test assertion. `test.log`/`build.log`/`lint.log` as committed predate this round's session (timestamped an hour before `run-e.json`'s `started_at`, i.e. from the prior deploy run before the owner's review) and so are not fresh proof for this diff's new tests; per the deferred-CI convention this is expected (the runner replaces them after the session ends) and is not treated as a defect, so the verdict rests on the static trace above plus the fix-response.md's own targeted-subset run (ruff/compileall clean, the new/changed tests passing in isolation from the sandbox's unrelated fixture-permission denial), not on the stale logs or any claude-*.json/run-*.json record (which belong to an earlier or still-open run).

Blast radius: confirmed the diff touches only plugin/gate/checks.py, plugin/lessons/index.py, plugin/commands/sdlc-maintain.md and three test files — no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml), no risk_list item, no schema or stored-data change; the hardening in `_read_text` also transitively protects the gate's own read of a supersedes target, which is a beneficial side effect rather than scope creep since it's the same function the owner named.

Policies: security-baseline relevant (path traversal / absolute-path escape in a gate check) — the fix closes the escape rather than papering over it (no longer echoes the target's raw parser-error text either, closing the information-leak half of the same finding); no stored personal data added; no new third-party dependency.

Tests: checked each new test's assertion actually depends on the fix (not satisfiable by the pre-fix code) by tracing the pre-fix `_supersedes_problem`/`_read_text`/`_month_label`/`_date_only` bodies from the diff's earlier (nested, pre-round) versions against the same inputs; found no case where the test would also pass against the old code. Noted one minor, non-blocking gap: no test exercises the 'supersedes target exists but is unreadable' branch's new (shorter, no-leak) message, but no test asserted the old longer message either, so this is a pre-existing coverage gap the round did not regress and the owner did not ask for.
